body.p: Applicant replies to the Office Action dated October 21, 2020, in which this Reply is filed within three months. Claims 1-20 stand rejected. Independent claims 1, 11, and 17 are currently amended. Dependent claims 2-10 are currently amended. Support for the present amendments can be found in the originally filed specification, claims, and drawings. Reconsideration is respectfully requested.

Claims 1-13, 15, and 16 are rejected under 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by U.S. Patent Publ. No. 2015/0232309 ("Jaipaul"). Applicant respectfully disagrees with the Examiner's rejections but amends claims 1 and 11 solely to expedite prosecution.
The Office Action recites on page 2 that Jaipaul discloses "the first cargo handing robot and the second cargo handling robot configured to move in two dimensions about a cargo deck."

Jaipaul recites in para. [0032], "FIG. 1 illustrates a wheel-engaging pneumatic lift system 20 having four individual pneumatic lifts 22 that receive compressed air from an overhead air distribution system 24. Compressed air from an external source can be supplied to the overhead air distribution system 24 via a supply line 26. The air in the supply line 26 can be split among distribution lines 28, which each supply compressed air to a respective one of the pneumatic lifts 22. Although FIG. 1 depicts two pair of pneumatic lifts 22, it should be noted that a single pair of pneumatic lifts 22 can be used to lift one end of a vehicle, while the other end remains on the ground. Further, for vehicles with more than four wheels, the pneumatic lift system 20 can include three or more pairs of pneumatic lifts 22 to match the total number of axles on the vehicle."
Jaipaul further recites in para. [0033], "the wireless handheld control module 30 can control raising, parking, and/or lowering of all of the pneumatic lifts 22 of the lift system 20."

In contrast, Applicant recites in para. [0029], "Movement mechanisms 31A and 31B may be configured to move first cargo handling robot 30A and second cargo handling robot 30B, respectively, about cargo deck 22. Movement mechanisms 32A and 32B may be configured to move first cargo handling robot 30A and second cargo handling robot 30B in a first direction (for example, in the X-direction) and a second direction (for example, in the Z-direction) and rotate first cargo handling robot 30A and second cargo handling robot 30B about the y-axis in a clockwise or counterclockwise direction. As such, in various embodiments, movement
mechanisms 31A and 31B may comprise any system capable of allowing translational movement along two dimensions."

Applicant amends claim 1 to recite, "...the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot configured to move in two dimensions about a cargo deck in response to receiving instructions from a control module" (emphasis added).

Applicant submits that Jaipaul fails to disclose or contemplate at least "the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot configured to move in two dimensions about a cargo deck in response to receiving instructions from a control module." For example, Jaipaul merely discloses four individual pneumatic lifts 22 that received compressed air from an overhead air distribution system 24 and a "wireless handheld control module 30 [that] can control raising, parking, and/or lowering of all of the pneumatic lifts 22 of the lift system 20." Thus, Jaipaul merely teaches lifting or lowering the lifts in a vertical direction (i.e., in one dimension) via the wireless handheld control module. In contrast, the claimed cargo handling robots of the present disclosure move in two dimensions about a cargo deck in response to receiving instruction from a control module.

Notwithstanding the above comments, Applicant further amends claims 1-10 to recite "an aircraft cargo handling system." Applicant submits that Jaipaul further fails to disclose or contemplate "an aircraft cargo handling system."

Claim 11 is amended, similar to claim 1, to recite, "...the movement mechanism is configured to transport the cargo unit from a first position to a second position along two dimensions in response to receiving instructions from a control module" (emphasis added). Applicant submits that the above comments regarding claim 1 apply, mutatis mutandis, to amended claim 11.

Applicant submits that Jaipaul fails to disclose or contemplate each and every aspect of amended independent claims 1 and 11. Thus, Applicant requests that the rejection under § 102 in view of Jaipaul be withdrawn.

Additionally, dependent claims 2-10, 12-13, and 15-16 variously depend from independent claims 1 or 11, and Applicant thus asserts that dependent claims 2-10, 12-13, and 15-16 are patentable for at least the same reasons for differentiating independent claims 1 and 11, as well as in view of their own respective features. Applicant respectfully requests that this rejection be withdrawn.
Rejections under Q 103
Claims 17-20 are rejected under 103 as being unpatentable over Jaipaul. Applicant respectfully disagrees with the Examiner's rejections but amends claim 17 solely to expedite prosecution.

Claim 17 is amended, similar to claim 1, to recite, "wherein the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot transport the cargo unit horizontally about a cargo deck in response to moving from the first position to the second position" (emphasis added). Applicant submits that the above comments regarding claim 1 apply, mutatis mutandis, to amended claim

Applicant submits that Jaipaul fails to disclose or contemplate each and every aspect of amended independent claim 17. Thus, Applicant requests that the rejection under § 103 in view of Jaipaul be withdrawn.

Additionally, dependent claims 18-20 depend from independent claim 17, and Applicant thus asserts that dependent claims 18-20 are patentable for at least the same reasons for differentiating independent claim 17, as well as in view of their own respective features. Applicant respectfully requests that this rejection be withdrawn. Claim 14
Claim 14 is rejected under 103 as being unpatentable over Jaipaul, in view of U.S. Patent No. 4,768,914 ("Sing"). Applicant traverses the rejection.

As previously discussed, Applicant submits that Jaipaul fails to disclose or contemplate each and every aspect of amended independent claim 11. Claim 14 depends from claim 11 so Applicant asserts that dependent claim 14 is patentable for at least the same reasons for differentiating independent claim 11, as well as in view of its own respective features. Applicant respectfully requests that this rejection be withdrawn.

In view of the above remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that all pending claims are allowable and requests allowance of the pending claims. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned at the Examiner's convenience, if that would help further prosecution of the subject application. Applicant authorizes and respectfully request that any fees due or
overpayments be charged or credited to Deposit Account No. 19-2814. This statement does NOT authorize payment of the issue fee.
